glossary.gallbladder: Small sac under the liver that stores and concentrates bile.
glossary.radiating: Pain spreading from its source to another area.
glossary.causative organism: The microbe responsible for the infection.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.percutaneous: Done through the skin, usually with a needle or tube under image guidance.
glossary.drainage: Removing fluid or pus through a tube or by surgery.
glossary.colicky: Pain that comes in waves as a hollow organ squeezes against a blockage.
glossary.diarrhoea: Loose or watery stools passed frequently.
glossary.jaundice: Yellow skin and eyes from raised bilirubin.
glossary.surgical drain: A tube left in after surgery to let fluid escape.
glossary.slipped clips: Surgical clips that have come off the cystic duct stump, letting bile leak.
glossary.cystic duct remnant: The short stump of cystic duct left after the gallbladder is removed.
glossary.iatrogenic: Caused by medical treatment or a procedure.
glossary.common hepatic duct: Duct draining bile from the liver; joins the cystic duct to form the common bile duct.
glossary.bile duct: Tube that carries bile from the liver and gallbladder to the duodenum.
glossary.abdominal ultrasound: Imaging of the abdomen with sound waves; first choice for the gallbladder.
glossary.gallbladder wall thickening: A thickened gallbladder wall on ultrasound, a sign of inflammation.
glossary.IV: Intravenous: given directly into a vein.
glossary.penicillin allergic: Allergic to penicillin-type antibiotics, so co-amoxiclav cannot be used.
glossary.bile: Fluid made by the liver that helps digest fat.
glossary.bile stasis: Bile sitting still instead of flowing, which encourages infection and stones.
glossary.mucosal: Relating to the inner lining of a hollow organ.
glossary.distension: Stretching or swelling of an organ.
glossary.ischaemia: Lack of blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.peritoneal irritation: Inflammation of the lining of the abdomen, causing pain on movement or pressure.
glossary.diaphragmatic descent: Downward movement of the diaphragm when breathing in.
glossary.inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as CRP and WCC that rise with inflammation or infection.
glossary.laparoscopic: Keyhole surgery done through small cuts using a camera.
